heading: Attention targeting (QK) and output writing (OV) explain much of GPT-2 small’s copy suppression
definition: the head's QK and OV circuits implement this suppression and explain most of its effect on loss (76.9% in the original).
summary: The original study supports this mechanism in GPT-2 small; no independent quantitative replication appears in the studies reviewed. The reported 76.9% measures KL divergence; the fraction of the loss effect recovered varies with how loss effects are combined.

suggested_status.by_scale: R0 at <1B (GPT-2 small only; counts record its size as 'not stated': versions.V2.studies_by_size = {not stated: 3}); no evidence at toy, 1-10B, 10-100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: The quantitative part (QK/OV-constrained ablation explaining 76.9% of L10H7's KL effect, r7) is reported by the original arXiv:2310.04625 on GPT-2 Small/OpenWebText and restated by its accompanying post lw:ebezsHW6qJwxTFasX, which the verdict did not count as a test (counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal.studies = 2). arXiv:2508.16109, a different author group (counts: versions.V2.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0), gives qualitative QK/OV inspection of head 10.7 on templated syllogism prompts, does not test the share, and received no V2 verdict (counts: versions.V2.studies_tested_without_verdict = 1). counts: versions.V2.verdicts supports/limits_scope/challenges all studies = 0; versions.V2.studies_by_family = {GPT-2: 3}; versions.V2.tested_with_uncertainty = 0. The original's own figures show loss-based recovery of 82% net and 45% absolute (r11, r12) and >50% KL recovery for many non-negative heads in layers 9-11 (Appendix J.3).
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent group re-running CSPA or another QK/OV-constrained ablation on GPT-2 small L10H7 and reporting KL and loss fractions would move this toward R2; the same in another family with copy-suppression heads would extend scope. An independent result that the loss-based fraction is low (as the original's 45% absolute-loss figure) or that the ablation recovers similar fractions for non-copy-suppression heads would bear on C for 'explain most of its effect on loss'. A V2 verdict on arXiv:2508.16109 would settle whether its QK/OV inspection counts as independent support of the mechanism part.

source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors inspected how L10H7’s query–key (QK) circuit directs attention and how its OV circuit maps attended tokens to outputs, and tested ablations on OpenWebText.
original_result.result: Compared with mean ablation, an ablation preserving the proposed copy-suppression mechanism explained 76.9% of L10H7’s effect on KL divergence. It recovered 82% of the net loss effect, which sums improvements and harms with their signs, and 45% of the absolute loss effect, which adds their sizes regardless of sign.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An independent measurement of the share of L10H7's effect explained by its QK and OV circuits (CSPA or any other mechanism-constrained ablation). The 76.9% figure appears only in the original and in its accompanying post, which the verdict did not count as a test.
untested.basis: arXiv:2508.16109 'untested parts of V2' line (the 76.9% share; no ablation constrained to the mechanism). counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal.studies = 2 (the pack shows these as arXiv:2310.04625 and lw:ebezsHW6qJwxTFasX, the latter marked NOT A TEST); versions.V2.verdicts.supports/limits_scope/challenges all have studies = 0.

untested.what: Full QK/OV mechanistic confirmation and CSPA recovery in models other than GPT-2 small, including GPT-2 Medium; weights-based testing in other families; comparisons across training stages or checkpoints. GPT-2 Medium already has a QK weights experiment, so weights-based testing beyond GPT-2 small is not wholly untested.
untested.basis: Checker correction for arXiv:2310.04625, Appendix B: repeats the Section 3.2 QK weights experiment in GPT-2 Medium, but reports no full QK/OV mechanistic confirmation or CSPA recovery there. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_family and .measurement.by_family both GPT-2 only; versions.V2.studies_by_size = {not stated: 3}; versions.V2.studies_by_stage = {not stated: 3}. The unspecified size and stage fields do not establish absence of the GPT-2 Medium experiment.

untested.what: Weight-based QK/OV analysis of L10H7 on ordinary or training-distribution text by a group other than the original's. arXiv:2508.16109's QK/OV inspection uses templated syllogism prompts.
untested.basis: arXiv:2508.16109 problems line (templated syllogism tasks, not ordinary text or the training distribution); counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.measurement.studies = 2.

untested.what: Uncertainty on the explained fractions (76.9% KL, 82% net loss, 45% absolute loss): no seeds, resamples or intervals reported.

wording_issues.phrase: explain most of its effect on loss (76.9% in the original)
wording_issues.issue: In the original, 76.9% is the fraction of L10H7's effect explained by CSPA measured in KL divergence relative to mean ablation on OpenWebText (r7), not loss. Loss-based measures in the same study give 82% of net loss effect recovered (r11) and 45% of absolute loss effect recovered (r12, state partial per verdict fix: well below the 76.9% KL figure). The accompanying post labels the 76.9% as 'performance recovery / fraction of L10H7 behavior explained' (r1).

Not in rows, from the original (Appendix J.3; Figure 17): CSPA-style QK/OV ablations recover more than 50% of KL for many non-negative heads in layers 9-11, which the pack says weakens the specificity of the 76.9% figure. A high recovered fraction under this ablation is thus not by itself specific to copy suppression.

wording_issues.phrase: the head's QK and OV circuits implement this suppression
wording_issues.issue: The QK evidence uses an idealized circuit (unembedding query, MLP0 effective-embedding key; 95.72%, r5), and the paper notes it does not fully f... (truncated). Not in rows (Appendix N): query-projection CSPA recovers only 25% of KL naively, and 61% with semantic subspaces plus learned per-token scale and bias. The pack's problems line also says the idealized QK setup d... (truncated).

method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2 Small L10H7, CSPA vs mean ablation on OpenWebText: 76.9% of effect explained in KL divergence (r7); 82% of net loss effect recovered (r11); 45% of absolute loss effect recovered (r12, state partial). The original's method-sensitivity line names KL versus loss-based metrics as a factor.

method_sensitivity.factor: which circuit the ablation preserves (QK only, OV only, both)
method_sensitivity.what: GPT-2 Small L10H7, OpenWebText, KL divergence relative to mean ablation: OV-only ablation 81.1% (r8), QK-only ablation 95.2% (r9), full CSPA with both 76.9% (r7).

CSPA explains 88.1% of L10H7's effect in the maximal percentile of completions ordered by mean-ablation KL effect (r10, Figure 5 groups completions into 100 percentiles) against 76.9% overall (r7). The original's method-sensitivity line says results depend on the behavioral sample selected (top 5% by L10H7 effect); its problems line says the behavioral result uses that selected sample, not an unselected distribution-wide one.

method_sensitivity.factor: input approximation (idealized vs more faithful query/key inputs)
method_sensitivity.what: QK diagonal result uses unembedding query and MLP0 effective-embedding key (95.72%, r5); a control with effective-embedding query changes the diagonal ranks (r6). Not in rows: query-projection CSPA recovers 25% of KL naively and 61% with semantic subspaces plus learned per-token scale and bias (Appendix N); keyside effective-embedding projection gives median attention change -0.09 against mean attention 0.21, and the context-free residual gives -0.06 (Appendix M.2). The original's method-sensitivity line names idealized versus more faithful input approximation.

In GPT-2 small, the reported role of head 10.7 changes across Simple, Opposite and Complex Syllogism formats (pack method-sensitivity line); the QK/OV rows on V2 come from the Opposite Syllogism task (r3, r4).
